title: Etale and Zariski cohomology agree for quasi-coherent sheaves
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $C$ a separated finite-type curve over $k$ of dimension at most one [def-sc-curves]. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_C$-module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent], let $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}$ be its associated sheaf on the small etale site [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. For every $q\geq0$ there is an isomorphism $H^q(C_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}})\cong H^q(C_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal F)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], [pqf-def-cohomology]. In particular, for the additive etale sheaf $\mathbf G_a=(\mathcal O_C)_{\mathrm{et}}$, one has $H^q(C_{\mathrm{et}},\mathbf G_a)\cong H^q(C,\mathcal O_C)$; both groups vanish for every $q\geq2$ when $C$ is a smooth connected curve.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-etale-zariski-qcoh-comparison] to X=C. Extract its family c and invert c(F,q). The comparison uses large Ext groups while this theorem uses the small Ext groups supplied by the Grothendieck abelian sheaf category. Identify these two Ext models additively by composing Mathlib Abelian.Ext.homAddEquiv in the two universes through the same standard derived category. Compose that identification with the inverse of c(F,q). This is the descent comparison of Stacks 03DW (2).

Use [def-sc-curves] to obtain LocallyOfFiniteType f, QuasiCompact f and topologicalKrullDim C ≤ 1. Mathlib LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian and QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace, the clauses recorded in [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], give IsLocallyNoetherian C and CompactSpace C because Spec k is Noetherian. Set F=Scheme.Modules.unit C and apply [lem-sc-zariski-dimension-bound] to its underlying abelian sheaf with d=1, using 1<2≤q. Apply [lem-sc-module-abelian-zariski-cohomology] to compare moduleCohomology with Sheaf.H' at the top open. AddCommGrpCat.subsingleton_of_isZero turns the dimension bound into subsingletonness, and the injectivity of the additive equivalence underlying the module/abelian comparison transfers it to moduleCohomology. This directly realizes the same 02UZ vanishing argument without passing through Scheme.Modules.H.

The associated sheaf of Scheme.Modules.unit C is the additive étale sheaf G_a by [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. Supply its quasi-coherence explicitly using SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent_unit. Specialize the comparison proved in step 1 to this module to prove etale_ga_cohomology_agree. For q≥2, use the injectivity of that additive equivalence to transfer the module cohomology subsingletonness established in step 2 to étale cohomology; return the pair of subsingleton proofs.

split_report.summary: The imported Cech proof was replaced by Stacks 03DW (etale/Zariski comparison for any quasi-coherent module on any scheme) and 02UZ (Noetherian topological dimension bounds Zariski sheaf cohomology). The former is already stated, more strongly and naturally, by lem-sc-etale-zariski-qcoh-comparison; the latter becomes the new unsplit node lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension, which matches the sorry theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.subsingleton_H_of_topologicalKrullDim_lt in slopmaster2. Since a finite-type curve over a field is Noetherian of dimension at most one, the vanishing applies to its structure sheaf; the associated etale sheaf is G_a. Statement made self-contained with its definitions and the stronger fact that all quasi-coherent modules vanish above degree one. No new Lean was written.

lean.statement: theorem etale_zariski_cohomology_agree {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve f] (F : C.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (q : ℕ) : Nonempty (Sheaf.H (Scheme.Modules.etaleTensorSectionsSheaf F) q ≃+ ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology C.toRingedSpace q).obj F))
lean.note: The three declarations give respectively the comparison for every quasi-coherent module, its structure-module (G_a) specialization, and both vanishings under the smooth connected curve hypothesis. Sheaf.H is the prescribed abelian-sheaf encoding of etale cohomology; RingedSpace.moduleCohomology is Zariski module cohomology. The unit module quasi-coherence proof is passed explicitly from the upstream theorem.
